why.line: It has the biggest moments: Ottilie re-lays every egg each time the clock strikes, Red-Mouth makes each egg three chicks, and the Bellows makes Herald of Spring's permanent +2/+2 land twice. Chicks start at 2/2 from turn one, so eggs feel good early and explode late, though most of the power lives inside the fight.

Chicks take a quarter of their host's stats, so the tribe feeds on the opponent's best units, and the sleepers give it real lasting growth: Old Unruh gains up to +12/+12 a fight, and you can tuck another tribe's carry to sleep beside a Warden. Cleaner and steadier than the winner, but early eggs off small hosts are tiny and its peaks are lower.

The idea of one clock that three builds want at different speeds is clever, and the Midsummer Leaver turning surviving chicks into lasting stats is a lovely payoff. But the numbers stay small (Ottilie gives +1/+1 three times at Tier 6), and chicks standing in the enemy's rows are hard to follow.

iteration_helped.line: Level, a little better: it stopped the clock striking over and over on its own, let Kasimir earn up to 2 gold, and let several Bellows stack, without losing any of its big combos.
Level: the chick rules are clearer, and the Egg-Painter now grows the Brood when an egg is lost, a small gain.
Slightly better: the Fledgling's chick hatches bigger, so early eggs matter, the Herald pays more gold on a fast clock, and sleepers are now plainly safe from every kind of targeting.
